scores.notes: Watercolor: God appears only as a white cloud with an orange flame at its heart above the tabernacle (top centre), with light inside the tent and Israelites at tent doors. Green-grey sky and ground wash reach all four borders.

Oil: a cloud column with fire glow over the path (top centre) has no figure in it; Moses with his staff leads a column carrying bundles between rearing walls of wave. Dark sea and rocks reach every edge.

Oil: a glowing human figure with a head, outstretched arms and a long robe stands in the light inside the smoke at the summit (upper centre-right). Otherwise Moses and the people are below the smoking mountain, and the painting reaches all edges.

Watercolor: the wash stops short of the left border and both top corners, leaving bare white paper along most of the left edge and in the top-left and top-right corners. The scene is correct: the Samaritan pours from a jug onto the shoulder wound, with linen and a flask on the ground and the donkey's reins loose.

Icon style: the Samaritan kneels and presses linen to the bleeding chest of the half-raised man, with a wine flask on a rock, a jug and linen strips on the ground and the donkey's reins loose (left). Gold sky and landscape reach all borders.

Oil: a veiled, ghostly standing figure with a hooded head and shoulders appears in the white glow above the flame on the summit (upper centre). Moses gestures to the people below, and the painting reaches all edges.

Watercolor: the Samaritan pours from a jug onto the man's chest wound with a cloth, and the donkey stands with its reins loose (right). Sky and rock washes reach all four borders; the pale patches on the left edge are painted rock highlights, not a margin.

Watercolor: the sky and ground washes fade into bare white paper at the left and right borders and both bottom corners, which is a vignette margin. The content is correct: God appears only as fire and cloud in the tabernacle, while Moses and Aaron hold the tally tablet and a kneeling father lifts a child.

Icon style: radiance, cloud and a small flame behind a luminous curtain (centre), with a patterned train of light spreading across the floor and no wearer or face. Isaiah with a staff and the priests are below, and the winged wall panels are temple decoration. Gold walls reach all edges.

Watercolor: a cloud with a flame in it (upper right) has no figure; Moses with his staff stands among crouched people gathering white flakes, with baskets and jars nearby. The dawn sky and ground are painted to every border.

Oil: dark smoke-cloud above the tabernacle, with flames pouring through the colonnade (centre) and no figure. The flames read somewhat like the tent burning rather than radiance filling it, so the scene match is partial. The camp rows reach all edges.

Oil: light rays and a flame descend from the cloud onto the tabernacle (upper centre) with no figure. Moses writes on the tablet beside Aaron in the breastplate while a father holds up a child, Levites carry poles, and Sinai stands at left. The painting is full-bleed.

Watercolor: the blue sky wash ends in a deckled edge short of the right border (upper right), and the sky fades to bare white paper at both side edges just above the horizon. The content is correct: God is only a cloud with fire, and Moses gestures over people gathering the flakes.

Icon style: a dark cloud with a column of fire and light enters the tabernacle (centre); the winged figures are woven cherubim on the curtains, not God. Priests and people stand around, and the painting reaches all edges.
Watercolor: a billowing cloud with a fire glow pours down onto the tabernacle (centre) with no figure, and Israelites stand at the tent doors at dusk. The washes reach every border.

Watercolor: a veiled, hooded standing figure with head and shoulders appears in the bright glow above the flame in the cloud (top centre). Moses leads the column between the walls of water, and the dark sky and water reach all edges.

Watercolor: smoke and fire erupt from the summit (top centre) with no figure, and rocks fly from the slopes. Moses with his staff stands in front of the gathered people, and the stormy sky washes reach all four edges.

Icon style: three child-sized figures at lower right have full adult beards and faces, a visible anatomy error. God appears only as cloud and flame, Moses and Aaron hold the tally tablet, and the gold ground reaches all edges.
Oil: the Samaritan kneels and pours from a jug onto the wounds of the half-raised, bare-chested man, with linen and a flask on the ground and the donkey standing by. The painting is full-bleed.

Icon style: a veiled, robed figure with a bearded face is visible inside the cloud above the flame on the mountain (upper centre). Moses and the people are below, and the gold ground reaches all edges.
Dark oil: flame and light inside the cloud above the sea (top centre) with no figure, and Moses leads the people between the walls of water at night. Dark paint reaches all four edges.

Oil: a column of light and a flame stand over the tabernacle (upper centre) with no figure. Moses marks the tablet beside Aaron while a father lifts a child, with Sinai behind, and the painting is full-bleed.
Watercolor: Moses (centre right) grips two separate staffs, one in each hand, which is a duplicated prop. God appears only as smoke and fire glow on the summit, and the washes reach all edges.
Oil: the cloud and light rays pour down and fire glows inside the tabernacle (centre) with no figure, while priests and people stand in the court. The painting is full-bleed.
Oil: a bright glow in the clouds (top centre) has no figure, and Moses with his staff gestures toward kneeling people among the white flakes, with baskets and jars. The painting is full-bleed.

Watercolor: the luminous train rises into a veiled, hooded standing human silhouette with head and shoulders under the fire-cloud (centre right), so the train is being worn by a figure. Isaiah and the priests are correct, and the washes reach all edges.
Oil: the Samaritan kneels and pours from a jug onto the bloodied man's shoulder, with linen and a jug on the ground and the donkey standing loose (right). The painting is full-bleed.

Oil: lettered captions read "What is it?" and "It is manna." at centre left and "It is manna." at centre right. God appears only as a flame-glow in the cloud (top centre), and the painting is full-bleed.

Watercolor: a flame in a halo of light above the clouds (top centre) has no figure, and the walls of water and the column are correct. Two near-identical white-bearded men with staffs and brown cloaks (lower centre-left and centre) read as a duplicated Moses.

Watercolor: the sky is left as bare white paper running off the top border and the upper left and right edges, and the washes fade to white at the side borders. The content is correct: God appears only as cloud and fire, Moses writes, Aaron is in the breastplate, and a father holds up a child.

Icon style: a beam of light and a flame descend under the dark cloud (top centre) with no figure, and Moses leads the people. The sea is drawn as low stepped cascades rather than towering walls of water, so the match is partial. The gold ground reaches all edges.

Icon style: a painted gold border frame runs around all four sides of the picture. Inside, God appears only as a cloud with a flame (top centre), and Moses points to the flakes while people gather them.

Watercolor: a veiled, robed human figure with arms and open hands outstretched stands in the light within the cloud at the far doorway (centre right). Isaiah stands with prostrate priests around him, and the washes reach all edges.

Dark oil: a flame on a floating brazier-like stand sits within the cloud, with a swirl of smoke down to the altar (centre) and no figure. No train fills the temple, so the match is partial. The painting is full-bleed.

Oil: a veiled, hooded standing figure with head, shoulders and folded arms rises in the light, its robe flowing down into the train (centre right). Isaiah and the priests are correct, and the painting is full-bleed.
